threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'thank you' to the bus driver. Locals just nod, like they're in a secret club. Welcome to Hackney!
Last night on the 50, a guy serenaded the whole bus with old school R&B. Only in Brixton does a random bus ride turn into a mini concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy serenading the tram passengers with an accordion, while everyone just nodded along—it hit me. This is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you see street performers in U-Bahn stations harmonizing with train announcements. It’s like an orchestral soundtrack to your morning commute.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You notice the real locals can name all the late-night food spots still open after a Giants game, while the transplants just ask for rides home.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling in front of a Muni stop while the bus was 20 minutes late. He was better entertainment than the bus would’ve been.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia's only about Gaudí and tapas, but it's the tiny art galleries and underground bars that really pulse with local life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the metro announcements—still scanning their phones instead of trusting the digital displays.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus at the stop, not realizing the 38 goes to the pub at the end of the street, not to the station.
Caught the N35 last night—two blokes arguing over the last chicken shop in Brixton, turns out they were mates from primary school.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a woman in a ball gown, chatting casually with a man in a tracksuit outside the Kiezkiosk at 3 AM. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings here, just follow the bass. No city matches that kind of underground vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate BART delays—calm and strategic, while newcomers are still visibly panicking at the announcements.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a guy on the 14 Mission shout 'I want my 5 minutes back!' as the bus sat stalled. Classic San Francisco frustration, but at least he had a sense of humor.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always assume the whole city runs on tapas. But in Gràcia, it’s all about the vermut and the afternoon stroll, not just the food.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they wait at the tram stops, fumbling with the ticket machine like it's an ancient artifact.
